modules.title: Spread and inside market
modules.lesson: A best bid of 5.00 and best offer of 5.04 imply a displayed four-cent spread, not a guaranteed four-cent execution cost. Depth may change before routing.
modules.fictional: At 5.00 x 400 and 5.04 x 250, an incoming market buy for 600 shares cannot assume the entire order fills at 5.04.
modules.predict: Which order-book information is missing to estimate the remainder?
modules.review: The next offer levels, venue/routing rules, queue dynamics, fees and possible hidden liquidity are unknown.
modules.transfer: Repeat with a two-cent quoted spread but only 30 shares at the best offer.

modules.title: Time and Sales color limits
modules.lesson: A green ask-side print or red bid-side print is a classification relative to contemporaneous quotes; it does not reveal a trader's intentions or predict price.
modules.fictional: Three trades print at the displayed ask, but the next quote steps lower.
modules.predict: Does ask-side execution prove sustained buying momentum?
modules.review: No. Trades show execution, not future order flow or a confirmed catalyst.
modules.transfer: Compare an at-bid print with a delayed quote update and explain classification uncertainty.

modules.title: VWAP arithmetic and inference
modules.lesson: VWAP equals summed price-times-volume divided by summed volume for a defined series and session.
modules.fictional: Two trades of 100 shares at $10 and 300 shares at $11 have VWAP = (1000+3300)/400 = $10.75.
modules.predict: Does a current quote above $10.75 mean most participants made money?
modules.review: No; VWAP is volume weighted, not a count of individual positions or realized profits.
modules.transfer: Calculate VWAP from three new hypothetical trades and state its limitations.

modules.title: EMA initialization and lag
modules.lesson: EMA uses smoothing coefficient alpha = 2/(N+1). EMA output depends on its prior initialized value.
modules.fictional: For N=9, alpha=0.2. A prior EMA of $10.00 and next close of $10.50 produce EMA = $10.10.
modules.predict: Does an EMA cross alone validate an entry?
modules.review: No; indicator lag, chop and volume/structure context matter; it is a descriptive input.
modules.transfer: Change N to 20 and calculate one update from the same starting EMA.

modules.title: Filing event and public cutoff
modules.lesson: Check the SEC filing item, acceptance timestamp, legal deadline and actual document; do not assume a Form 8-K always precedes a press release.
modules.fictional: A company releases news at 8:00 AM and its related filing becomes available later; a forum says the announcement is automatically illegal.
modules.predict: What official rule and facts must be established before reaching that conclusion?
modules.review: Confirm event category, applicable deadline and disclosure exceptions from primary authority; avoid legal conclusions from chronology alone.
modules.transfer: Audit a different dated release with incomplete filing information.

modules.title: Financing authorization versus proceeds
modules.lesson: An approved offering or shelf capacity is not necessarily issued securities, deposited proceeds or revenue.
modules.fictional: A fictional issuer registers potential issuance up to $20 million but reports no completed sales in the provided records.
modules.predict: Can the learner describe $20 million in cash as received?
modules.review: No; verify terms, issuance, actual sales and net proceeds using separate dated disclosures.
modules.transfer: Evaluate a rights offering with conditional participation.
